codes.label: Salience following
codes.definition: Correlation of weekly issue shares between an outlet and the core set
decision_rules: a story belongs to an issue when its title or text matches the issue's query terms (Appendix A): Ukraine — Ukraine OR Ukrainian OR Kyiv OR Kiev OR Zelensky OR (Russia AND invasion); Gaza — Gaza OR Hamas OR (Israel AND (war OR strike OR ceasefire OR hostages)); COP — COP27 OR COP28 OR (climate AND (summit OR conference) AND (Sharm OR Dubai OR UNFCCC)); terms fixed before retrieval and tested on a pilot week per outlet
issue share = stories matching the issue query / all stories of the outlet that week
issue share = issue stories ÷ all stories of the outlet that week (Media Cloud weekly count)
weeks with fewer than 5 outlet stories are dropped

codes.label: Frame
codes.definition: The dominant generic frame of the article
examples: Episodic: a single event or person, no wider context
Conflict: disagreement between parties is the organizing idea
Responsibility: attributes cause or solution to an actor
Human interest: a family's escape from Kharkiv leads the story
Economic consequences: wheat prices rise after the Black Sea deal ends
Thematic: the lead places the day's strike in the war's two-year course
decision_rules: code the frame of the headline and lead paragraph, for every outlet (core and peripheral) and for agent-written proposals
one dominant frame per article; 'other' if none fits
agents assign one codebook frame to each proposed item; 300 written-out proposals are coded by the model coder to check the labels
read the headline first, then the lead paragraph; when they differ, the lead decides
when two frames are present, code the one the headline states; if the headline states none, the one the lead's first sentence states
episodic vs thematic: code thematic only when the lead itself gives background, a trend or a cause

categories.label: Episodic
categories.definition: Reports a single event, incident or person, with no wider background, trend or cause.

categories.label: Thematic / context
categories.definition: Places the event in a wider context: background, trends, causes, history or policy.

categories.label: Conflict
categories.definition: Disagreement or confrontation between parties, sides or countries is the organizing idea.

categories.label: Human interest
categories.definition: A personal or emotional angle: individuals' experiences, suffering or stories lead.

categories.label: Responsibility
categories.definition: Attributes the cause of, or the solution to, the problem to an actor (government, group, person).

categories.label: Economic consequences
categories.definition: Costs, prices, trade, aid money, markets or other economic effects lead.

categories.label: Other
categories.definition: None of the six fits the headline and lead.

codes.label: Timing
codes.definition: V3a: lag in days from the first core story to the first outlet story on the same event, entered as the negative lag; V3b: lag in weeks of the peak cross-correlation of weekly issue shares, entered as the negative lag
decision_rules: an event is a GDELT event record; a story is matched to an event through the article URLs GDELT links to that event (mentions table)
lags above 14 days are censored
higher (less negative) values mean closer following

codes.label: Wire reliance
codes.definition: share of an outlet's sampled foreign stories that credit AP, AFP or Reuters, or that share at least 50% of their text with an AP, AFP or Reuters story published in the three days before
decision_rules: credit in byline, dateline or end note counts
text reuse: document similarity to AP, AFP and Reuters stories published on the agencies' public sites within 3 days before; threshold 50% of the story's text, checked against the hand-coded credits
credits to national or non-Western agencies are coded under C10, not here

foreign story = sampled story datelined outside the outlet's country or credited to a foreign source (a wire or agency based in another country); when the text shows neither a dateline nor a credit, the place where the reported events mainly take place decides (a statement or decision: where it was made if stated, else the main actor's country). Revised October 6, 2026 under the plan's if_below rule (model self-consistency alpha .782 < .80 with the first wording); author's choice 'Event location'.
identification (X10): dateline and credit by rule (data/analysis/code_rules.py); event location by the model coder (prompt version 2) when the rule finds neither

categories.label: not a foreign story (C4, C8, C10 only)

codes.label: Tier
codes.definition: World-system position of the outlet's country
decision_rules: Gunaratne (2001) index: [(% of world GNP × 0.55) + (% of world exports × 0.45)], World Bank data for 2022
the three higher-scoring sampled countries form the semi-periphery (declared departure from a published classification, author ruling of September 29, 2026); scores recorded with the citation

2022 scores (D1; X1): India 2.83, Malaysia 0.66, Nigeria 0.44 → semi-periphery; South Africa 0.41, Bangladesh 0.34, Kenya 0.09 → periphery; Nigeria's exports from BX.GSR.GNFS.CD (NE.EXP.GNFS.CD null); values in data/coded/v5_tier.csv

codes.label: Local stake
codes.definition: Issue-level stake for the sampled countries
decision_rules: fixed a priori by issue: Ukraine 0 (low), Gaza 1 (mixed), COP27/COP28 2 (high)
robustness: two dummy contrasts; V10 (C9) as an outlet-level check
country × issue stake (check within the wars): coded a priori by the two human coders from each country's diplomatic, economic and population ties to the issue, on the same 0/1/2 scale
X14 (October 6, 2026): no country × issue stake is coded — the within-wars check is dropped; nothing in the study is hand-coded

codes.label: Simulated following
decision_rules: same formulas as C1–C3, on the second half of each issue's period
agents' frame labels are coded with C2 by the same model coder as the observed articles

codes.label: Correspondent presence
codes.definition: The article is a foreign story filed by the outlet's own staff from abroad
examples: staff byline with a dateline outside the outlet's country
decision_rules: wire-credited or syndicated stories count as not own staff
a staff byline with a home-country dateline does not count

categories.label: not a foreign story (C4, C8, C10 only)

codes.label: Own-country mention
codes.definition: The story names the outlet's own country in its title or text
examples: a Nairobi outlet's COP28 story that names Kenya
decision_rules: country name, demonym or capital counts
dateline alone does not count

categories.label: not a foreign story (C4, C8, C10 only)

codes.label: National-agency credit
codes.definition: The article credits a national news agency or a non-Western international agency
examples: BSS (Bangladesh), KNA (Kenya), NAN (Nigeria), PTI (India), SAnews (South Africa), Bernama (Malaysia), Xinhua
decision_rules: credit in byline, dateline or end note counts
an article crediting both a national agency and AP, AFP or Reuters is coded under both C4 and C10

categories.label: not a foreign story (C4, C8, C10 only)

note: Stage 6b: C2 categories and tie rules completed from plan V7; C5 filled from D1 under X1.
